question: Round 3 Bind, lost pistol + bonus, ATK bank ~1900cr each. DEF are full-buy. What's the team call?

options.label: Full save: pistols + minimal util, group up for a close-range stack on one site and play for the next full-buy
options.explication_courte: Saving guarantees a full-buy (rifle + heavy shields + util) next round. A grouped pistol stack on one site creates a round-steal chance without torpedoing the eco.

options.label: Coordinated half-buy: SMG (Spectre) + light shields for everyone, fast-hit surprise on one site
options.explication_courte: A Spectre light-shield force at ~1900-2400cr can surprise defenders, but if you lose it leaves the team in semi-buy next round instead of a guaranteed full-buy.

sources_option.citation: If you all have roughly 2200-2400 credits each it might be worth forcing Spectre light shields to catch your opponents off guard.

options.label: Everyone buys a Sheriff + light shields and spreads out to fish for long-range picks at entry points
options.explication_courte: Spreading out on a Sheriff eco dilutes your firepower: every isolated duel against rifles is losing. Eco rounds are won through grouping, not spreading.

sources_option.citation: To maximize eco impact, group up and play close-range together; spreading out into long-range duels against full rifles loses the weapon-disadvantaged fights.

options.label: Uncoordinated partial buy: 2 players grab a Vandal, the other 3 stay on pistol with no shared plan
options.explication_courte: A split buy breaks the whole team's eco without enough firepower to back it up: 2 isolated rifles don't win, and the other 3 won't have a full-buy next round either.

sources_option.citation: The safest strategy after a lost round is a complete save so the team can full-buy together next round; a partial uncoordinated buy wastes credits without firepower.

explication_longue:
Situation: round 3 on Bind, your team lost the pistol and the bonus round, every player is sitting on ~1900 credits, defenders are full-buy. This is a team economy decision, not a positioning one.

The core eco principle: don't spend credits that stop you from full-buying next round. At ~1900cr, nobody can afford a rifle + heavy shields + util. The safest line is a full save: buy only pistols (Sheriff/Ghost) and minimal util, group up for a close-range stack on one site, and play for the guaranteed full-buy in round 4. A grouped pistol stack can steal the round if defenders over-extend, without ever compromising the economy.

A force buy (Spectre + light shields) becomes rational closer to 2200-2400cr to catch opponents off guard — that's an acceptable option, but it breaks the eco and leaves the team in semi-buy if they lose. Spreading out on an eco round (costly option) is a classic mistake: eco power comes from grouping and close-range combat, never from isolated long-range duels against rifles. The uncoordinated split buy is the mistake: it burns everyone's credits without enough firepower.

Estimated elite distribution: ~54% full save grouped, ~26% coordinated Spectre force, ~15% spread out on Sheriff (costly), ~5% uncoordinated split buy (the mistake). GTO tolerance: full save and coordinated force are both defensible depending on exact bank and score; spreading and the split buy are the errors.

sources.citation: The standard play after losing a round is a complete save so you can buy rifles, Heavy Shields and utility next round; force Spectre light shields only around 2200-2400cr.
Maximize eco chances by grouping up and playing close-range together, taking surprise duels or stacking a site to offset the weapon disadvantage.
The safest strategy is to eco and save for a full buy next round; not saving risks not affording heavy shields plus a rifle the round after.

_gaps.incertitude: La banque exacte (~1900cr) place ce round a la frontiere save/force ; a 2200cr+ l'option 'force Spectre' pourrait devenir optimale. Le seuil precis depend du reglage des recompenses de round et du score, non specifie.
Frequences estimees depuis guides d'economie (boosteria, mobalytics, ldshop) ; les vrais pourcentages varient selon le meta pro/ranked et le round exact.
Les positions au spawn ATK sont schematiques (decision d'achat prise au buy phase, pas de contact) ; un juge pourrait estimer que le choix depend surtout du score de manche (ex: 0-2 vs 5-7).
